nodes.question: What is the main focus of the systematic review by Chatzigeorgiou and Andreou (2021)?
nodes.answer: The review examines feedback research for residential energy behaviors through mobile and web interfaces.
nodes.paragraph: "Discussions" discusses the findings. Sect. "Limitations and Further Research" outlines the study S limitations and proposes direc- tions for future research. Finally, Sect. "Conclusion" summarizes the findings and broader implications for the field. Background App-based energy feedback and user engagement App-based energy feedback has emerged as a prom- ising digital solution to enhance user awareness and engagement with energy usage. A systematic review by Chatzigeorgiou and Andreou, (2021) examined feedback research for residential energy behaviours Energy Efficiency (2025) 18:25 25 Vol. : (123456789) through mobile and web interfaces, highlighting the need for more comprehensive studies on these solu- tions long-term impacts and scalability. Smart energy apps offer context-specific feed- back that allows users to track and reflect on their consumption patterns (Hermsen et al., 2016). This feedback can assist users in exploring manage- ment strategies, yet the extent to which these apps shape sustainable energy practices within house- holds remains under-researched and still limited to pilot-level projects (Attour et al., 2020; Geelen et al., 2019; Murugesan et al., 2015; Valor et al., 2019).
